rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE MEMBERS OF THE AGRARIAN REFORM ADJUDICATION BOARD, AMENDING SECTION 13 OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 129-A, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REORGANIZATION ACT OF THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRARIAN REFORM, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Department of Agrarian Reform Adjudication Board (DARAB), created under Executive Order No. 129-A, is the quasi-judicial body with the primary jurisdiction of hearing and determining all agrarian disputes except those pertaining to the determination of just compensation and resolution of criminal offenses arising from the implementation of agrarian laws.  DARAB, however, is confronted with an enormous backlog of cases.  To date, there are approximately 9,000 pending cases on agrarian disputes, about one-third (1/3) of which are on appeal. Given the increasing volume of agrarian cases, it appears that the present composition of the DARAB, and its procedure for resolving appealed cases in no longer adequate.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 2001-09-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE DRUG ENFORCEMENT ADMINISTRATION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6425, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) shall merge the functions of separatae drug law enforcement agencies.  Its mission is to enforce the controlled substances laws and regulations of the Philippines and bring to the criminal and civil justicesustem of the State, or any other competent jurisdiction, those organizations and principal members of organizations, involved in the growing, manufacture, or distribution of controlled substances appearing in or destined for illicit traffic on the Philippines. The DEA shall recommend and support non-enforcement programs aimed at reducing the availability of illicit controlled substances on the domestic and international markets.

rows.abstract: Absentee Voting/Absentee Voter. Absentee voting applies to any citizen residing abroad who has all the qualifications and none of the disqualificatio n of a voter, hereinafter called the absentee voter.  He shall have the right to vote in any national or local election by absentee ballot in the city or municipality where he last resided prior to his departure from the Philippines.

rows.abstract: There shall be established in capital towns and cities of the Philippine an Armed Forces of the Philippines Perosnnel Retirement and Separation Processing Offices to be determined by the Secretary of National Defense which offices shall be vested with the full authority to process all claims for retirement and separation benefits in accordance with existing laws.

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING MEDICAL ETHICS BY REPEALING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 169, AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 212, WHICH REQUIRES ANY ATTENDING PHYSICIAN OF ANY HOSPITAL, MEDICAL CLINIC, SANITARIUM OR OTHER MEDICAL ESTABLISHMENTS OR ANY MEDICAL PRACTITIONER WHO HAS TREATED ANY PERSON FOR SERIOUS OR LESS SERIOUS PHYSICAL INJURIES TO REPORT THE FACT OF TREATMENT
rows.abstract: Rationale: The obligation imposed by Executive Order 212 upon medical practitioners to report cases of physical injuries, tends to discourage them from carrying on their medical functions because of the risk that they might be implicated in the process. As a result, medical practitioners who are in a position to help those in need hesitate to do so.> To eliminate the apprehension felt by medical practitioners because of the requirement in law, this bill seeks to repeal P.D. 169, as amended by Executive Order 212. This will enable our physicians to pursue the vows set forth in the Hippocratic Oath whereby all those in need are to be treated regardless of class, creed or ideology.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-09-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING CENTERS FOR STREET CHILDREN IN EVERY REGION OF THE PHILIPPINES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: There shall be established in every region in the Philippines, centers for street children which shall extend services to all exploited infants and children, mendicant children, dependent, abandoned, vagrant and neglected children, and youth offenders covered by Presidential Decree Numbered Six Hundred and Three, as amended. The Center shall be under the direct supervision of the Department of Social Welfare and Development.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2001-09-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE BUREAU OF DISTANCE EDUCATION AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: For the purpose of this Act, distance education is defined as an educational process in which a significant portion of the teaching is conducted outside of the confined of the formal classroom set-up where student-teacher contact is normally required, and such contact is effected through communicaiton with the aid of printed visual materials video, radio or other similar means of communication.> There is hereby created the Bureau of Distance Education in the Department of Education, Culture andSports, which shall be charged with the responsibility of formulating policies and guidelines, and coordinating and monitoring the curricula, activities and functions of all corresponding schools with a view to ensuring their effectiveness in providding quality education.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-09-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER STRENGTHENING THE PHILIPPINE BANKING SYSTEM, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE `THE NEW CENTRAL BANK ACT' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to STRENGTHEN the banking system with these significant amendments to RA No. 7653, such as: (1) LOWERS the term of office of the members of the Bangko Sentral Monetary Board from [six (6)] to THREE (3) years; (2) INCREASES the frequency of bank examinations; (3) IMPOSES COLLATERAL (shares of bank owners) in cases of loans granted to provide liquidity; and (4) Authorizes the Monetary Board to order INQUIRY into all deposits worth P50 Million or its equivalent in foreign currency;etc.

rows.author: D023
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR DEBT-RELIEF MEASURES TO REHABILITATE FINANCIALLY DISTRESSED ENTERPRISES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Corporate Recovery Act". Rationale: Many businesses are now in the dumps, and are hoping for the enactment of a measurwith a comprehensive approach to the complex problems that beset them, especially when they can no longer pay their outstanding obligations as they come due. Their debts, in other words, is their most immediate concern.> Adjudication of cases involving financially distressed companies were based on the out-dated Insolvency Law passed in 1909 and the suspension of payments and rehabilitation provisions in the Presidential Decree 902-A. However, while the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has recently adopted rules governing petitions for suspension of payment and rehabilitation of financially distressed companies, itts has been hampered by inadequacy of laws concerning such cases. Lacking a set of procedural rules to govern these cases, the courts too have no choice but to apply the antiquated procedures of the Insolvency Law.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECONOMIC AFFAIRS since 2001-09-27

rows.author: D020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR AN INCREASE IN THE SALARIES OF PUBLIC OR GOVERNMENT SECTOR EMPLOYEES AND IN THE STATUTORY MINIMUM WAGE AND SALARY RATES OF EMPLOYEES AND WORKERS IN THE PRIVATE SECTOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: All workers and employees in the public and government sector shall receive an increase of ten percent (10%) in their monthly salaries. > The statutory minimum wage rates of workers and employees in the private sector shall be increased by One Hundred Twenty-Five Pesos (P125.00) per day. Provided, that those already receiving above the minimum wage shall have an increase of One Hundred Twenty Pesos (P120.00) per day.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2001-09-27

rows.abstract: The bill seeks to increase retirement benefits and shorten the required length of service in the government. Under this proposed measure, monthly pensions are computed based on the highest monthly salary, highest monthly longevity pay and highest monthly aggregate of transportation, living , and representation allowances at the time of retirement, resignation or death. rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY TO PROMOTE THE VIABILITY AND GROWTH OF COOPERATIVES AS INSTRUMENTS OF EQUITY, SOCIAL JUSTICE AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, DEFINING ITS POWERS, FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIE S, RATIONALIZING GOVERNMENT POLICIES AND AGENCIES WITH COOPERATIVE FUNCTIONS, SUPPORTING COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT, TRANSFERRING THE REGISTRATION AND REGULATION FUNCTIONS OF EXISTING GOVERNMENT AGENCIES ON COOPERATIVES AS SUCH AND CONSOLIDATING THE SAME WITH THE AUTHORITY, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

Rationale: RA No. 6939 created the COOPERATOVE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY in 1990 despite the dedication and valiant efforts of its officials and personnel, particularly those assigned to man its various Extension Offices, the Authority has encountered tremendous difficulties and obstacles in the pursuit of its mission to promote the viability and growth of cooperatives.> The reason lies in the failure of Republic Act No. 6939 to provide the authority the adequate development and regulatory powers, not to mention adequate financial resources.> The bill seeks to strengthen the development and regulatory powers of the CDA in order to ensure that the Authority will be more responsive to tthe challenges of the future. Thus, the bill introduced the concept of Cooperatives Development Council and the Cooperative Adjudicatory Board in the CDA.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2001-09-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING RETIREMENT BENEFITS TO ELECTIVE AND APPOINTIVE BARANGAY OFFICIALS
rows.abstract: In addition to the benefits granted to barangay officials under existing laws and regulations, the Punong Barangay, Barangay Kagawad, President of Sangguniang Kabataan, Barangay Treasurer and Barangay Secretary, as well as other barangay officials and workers who may hereafter be mandatorily elected or appointed by provision of law, who have rendered a total of ten (10) years or more of government service, six (6) of which as barangay official or worker, shall be ENTITLED FOR LIFE TO A MONTHLYRETIREMENT PENSION in the amount of one-half of his last honorarium or highest monthly honorarium, whichever is higher.

rows.abstract: Rationale: It is the duty of the government to protect both persons and properties from damage hence, it may use its police power to impose measures in order to achieve this objective. rows.abstract: Public school teachers are among the most underpaid workers in our society.  The low salaries received by our public school teachers have been a major disincentive for them to improve their skills in teaching and pursue further education and training.  In addition, the public schools have failed to attract the best and the brightest students from the top colleges and universities because of the low salary levels, preventing our public education system from benefiting from the knowledge and expertise of qualified teachers.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE AIR FORCE ACADEMY (PAFA) AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Women victims are often forced to endure situations of violence due to the lack of services that will support the decision to resist violence. This problem is very prominent among victims, or survivors, of domestic violence who feels theneed to leave their homes but are restrained from doing so by the absence or lack of financial resources, child care support and shelter.  Many actually think that they do not have much choice in the situation but to suffer in silence and solitude, resulting in serious physical and psychological consequences. > This Act shall be known as "Women and Children Crises Survivors Assistance and Protection Act of 2001".
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 2001-09-27

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 334 OF ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE(RE: CONCUBINAGE)
rows.abstract: Although both the crimes of adultery and concubinage violate marriage vows, the law treats them differently. A married woman can already be convicted of adultery by a single act of sexual intercourse. While the husband can be convicted of concubinage only if sexual intercourse was performed under scandalous circumstances, or if he does any of the two other acts specified in the Revised Penal Code. Therefore, the law makes the crime of concubinage more difficult to establish. The law also imposes a lesser penalty for the crime of concubinage. >This Act seeks to remedy such inequality in the law by amending Article 334 of the Revised Penal Code. The amendment deletes the phrase "under scandalous circumstances", increases the penalty and quallifies the penalty to be imposed on the concubine.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-09-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD AS A SEPARATE AND DISTINCT SERVICE ATTACHED TO THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS, FURTHER AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 5173, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Philippine Coast Guard Law of 2001". Rationale: The US Coast Guard (USCG) is a military service and a branch of the armed forces of the United States at all times EXCEPT when operating as a service in the Navy, the USCG becomes a service in the Department of Transportation. This would be the closest model (among other several models of foreign countries) on maritime safety administration organization to our Philippine Coast Guard (PCG).  In times of peace, the PCG shall be under the DOTC.  Butin times of war or national emergencies, it shall be placed under the operational control of the Department of National Defense to render services.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06478

rows.abstract: This bill states that RAPE is committed by any other person who, under any of the circumstances mentioned in paragraph 1 hereof shall commit an act of sexual assault by inserting his penis into another person's mouth or anal orifice or any instrument or object OR OTHER PARTS OF THE BODY into the genital or anal orifice of another EXCEPT WHEN THE PERSON IS PERFORMING MEDICAL, CLINICAL OR SCIENTIFIC DUTY OR OTHER PROFESSIONAL OBLIGATION AND WITH THE CONSENT OF THE VICTIM.

rows.abstract: This bill which seeks to punish and eradicate anti-money laundering activities in the country - implements the declared policy of the State to provide the necessary legal and policy environment for the domestic and international markets to enable the government to protect and promote legitimate business capital and interests and enhance the flow of legitimate financial transactions in the country. It is consistent with objectives of government to punish economic crimes and those who benefit from the proceeds of these economic crimes - all these as a significant step to protect and safeguard the integrity of our financial system.

rows.author: D036
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING EXEMPTION TO THE PROSECUTORS OF THE NATIONAL PROSECUTION SERVICE, STATE COUNSELS OF THE OFFICE OF THE CHIEF STATE COUNSEL OF THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE, LAWYERS OF THE OFFICE OF THE OMBUDSMAN, AND PUBLIC ATTORNEYS OF THE PUBLIC ATTORNEY'S OFFICE FROM THE COVERAGE OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6758, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE SALARY STANDARDIZATION LAW
rows.abstract: Rationale: This proposal comes at a time when we can no longer ignore the demands of the situation.  If the government truly means business in its fight against criminality, it must start from the basic.  The compensation package for the Public andSpecial Prosecutors as well as the Public Attorneys has to be reviewed, and the first legal obstacle that has to be addressed is the Salary Standardization Law (R.A. 6758). This measure seeks the exemption of the Prosecutors of the National Prosecution Service, the State Counsels of the Office of the Chief State Counsel, the Public Attorneys of the Public Attorney;s Office, and the Lawyers of the Office of the Ombudsman from the coverage of said Act, with the intention of setting a new compensattion package which will be commensurate to the functions that they perform and comparable with those being received by their counterparts in the private sector.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING INDUSTRIES ENGAGED IN THE EXPLOITATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES TO GIVE PREFERENTIAL EMPLOYMENT TO LOCAL RESIDENTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to provide employment in communities where extractive industries are engaged in the development and exploitation of natural resources. More often than not, these extractive industries such as mining, quarrying, cement manufacture, logging, generation for power by steam (geothermal) or water (hydro-electric ) cart off the national wealth without even sharing their profits in the form of benefits with local residents.  In fact, in most cases, these extractive industries, after they had taken away the natural wealth of these communities, left these communities poorer than before the extraction of their wealth.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-09-27
